title: Maximisation bias, double Q-learning, and Expected SARSA
brief: Measure the upward bias of a max over noisy estimates, remove it with the double estimator and double Q-learning, and run Expected SARSA at a step size of one on the cliff.
hints: double_estimate is np.take_along_axis(means_b, np.argmax(means_a, axis=-1)[..., None], axis=-1)[..., 0].
For epsilon_greedy_probs, best = q_row == q_row.max(), then epsilon / A + (1 - epsilon) * best / best.sum().
Double Q-learning's target is r + gamma * Q2[s2][argmax Q1[s2]] when updating Q1. Using max(Q2[s2]) is the single estimator again.
Act on Q1[s] + Q2[s], and draw a fresh coin with rng.random() < 0.5 after every step to pick which table to update.
MaxBiasMDP tables are lists of rows, so index them as Q[s][a], not Q[s, a].
